claims.text: The adapter -- not the caller -- renders the evidence blocks, because a gate that only REPORTS withheld paths while the caller ships the bytes anyway is worse than no gate: it produces a record saying the council did not see a file it did in fact see.  Withheld files are named but their contents are never rendered.
claims.why: Code shows evidence_files loop skips blocked paths; evidence_paths only adds path names, not contents. Withheld files are listed in a separate section without content.

claims.text: FLOOR FIRST, on the raw caller inputs, before anything is assembled: the runner must not be reachable from a refused call.
claims.why: floor_check is called before assemble and before any dispatch; if refusal is not None, returns early without invoking runner.

claims.text: The runner is NOT invoked. The secret never leaves the process, and the recorded reason names the rule, never the bytes.
claims.where: ask method comment in refusal branch
claims.why: When refusal is not None, returns _reply with status='refused_by_floor' and reason=refusal.rule; no dispatch call.

claims.text: Charged BEFORE dispatch from the assembled prompt: a per-call timeout does not bound token spend, and reconciling after the call is not a budget.
claims.where: ask method comment for token ceiling
claims.why: Token counting and ceiling check occurs before _dispatch call; if over ceiling, returns early without dispatch.

claims.text: a vendor must never take the council down
claims.where: ask method comment in except clause
claims.why: Exception is caught broadly and returns an error VendorReply, preventing crash.

claims.text: ALWAYS read-only.  There is no constructor switch for the sandbox mode: a reviewer that can write is not a reviewer, and an option is a thing someone sets.
claims.why: No code in this chunk enforces read-only sandbox; the claim is about the adapter's behavior but no implementation details are present.
